blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the advanced level, demand and supply are understood as dynamic systems that interact in ways a simple forecast can never capture. Price shifts change demand. Stock levels change customer behaviour. A promotion reshapes the curve, and a competitor's move changes the baseline. A single forecast, however precise, is always a snapshot of a system that does not stand still.

The senior planner thinks in curves and elasticities, not in single numbers. What happens to demand if we raise the price five per cent? What happens if a competitor lowers theirs? How does a promotion cannibalise future demand, and by how much? What is the risk that today's stock-out becomes tomorrow's lost customer?

What matters at this level is not predicting the exact number, but understanding the shape of the response — so that when reality unfolds differently from plan, the team can adjust with confidence rather than panic. It is the same difference as between a weather forecast and a pilot's ability to fly through unexpected weather. The forecast helps; the skill of the pilot decides whether the plane lands safely.

items.q: According to the text, why is a single forecast always limited?
options: It is a snapshot of a system that does not stand still
It ignores the competitor's price entirely
It is calculated with outdated data
It is too optimistic about demand
items.why: "A single forecast, however precise, is always a snapshot of a system that does not stand still."

items.q: How does the senior planner primarily think about demand?
items.why: "The senior planner thinks in curves and elasticities, not in single numbers."

items.q: What does the text say matters most at the advanced level?
options: Understanding the shape of the response
items.why: "What matters at this level is not predicting the exact number, but understanding the shape of the response."

items.q: The pilot analogy suggests that the author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: A precise enough forecast removes the need for adjustment
Judgement matters when reality diverges from plan
Conditions can change after the forecast is made
items.why: Inferência: a analogia diz que a perícia do piloto — não a previsão — decide o pouso; nenhuma previsão dispensa o ajuste.

items.q: The reference to a promotion that "cannibalises future demand" suggests that…
options: promotions have no effect on the curve
a gain in sales now can be borrowed from later periods
items.why: Inferência: canibalizar demanda futura implica que a venda de hoje pode estar sendo puxada de amanhã, não somada a ela.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie orientando um planejador sênior. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, before you build the launch forecast, I want you to resist the temptation to treat this as a clean addition of demand. It won't be. What this launch really does is compete with our existing line, not just create a new market.

Here is what I'd flag first. Some of the volume you'll book as new is almost certainly demand you were going to capture anyway, through the current product. That's cannibalisation, and if you don't model it explicitly, the launch will look wildly more successful than it is — until the existing line's numbers start sliding.

What I want from you is not a single point estimate. Give me the curve. What happens if we price a little above the old line? A little below? Where does the cannibalisation get painful? And keep half an eye on supply — if we sell through faster than planned, a stock-out on day ten turns an early win into an angry customer.

Honestly, the exact number matters far less than knowing the shape of the response. If you understand the shape, you can adjust the moment reality diverges from the plan — and it will diverge.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is the main risk Sophie wants the planner to avoid?
options: Setting the launch price too low
Treating the launch as a clean addition of demand
items.why: "resist the temptation to treat this as a clean addition of demand… What this launch really does is compete with our existing line."

items.q: According to Sophie, what happens if cannibalisation is not modelled explicitly?
options: The competitor will copy the launch
The launch will look more successful than it really is
The forecast will be too pessimistic
items.why: "the launch will look wildly more successful than it is — until the existing line's numbers start sliding."

items.q: What does Sophie ask the planner to deliver instead of a single point estimate?
options: The curve of the response at different prices
items.why: "What I want from you is not a single point estimate. Give me the curve."

items.q: Why does Sophie mention a stock-out on day ten?
options: To explain how to price the product
To warn that selling through faster than planned can turn an early win into a lost customer
To argue that supply is more important than demand
To recommend holding more inventory permanently
items.why: Inferência: ela liga a venda rápida à ruptura de estoque, que transforma o sucesso inicial num cliente insatisfeito.

items.q: What does Sophie imply with "and it will diverge"?
options: The team should not bother forecasting at all
The forecast is likely to be wrong in every detail
The competitor will certainly undercut the price
Reality departing from the plan is expected, so readiness to adjust matters
items.why: Inferência: ela trata o desvio como inevitável, por isso valoriza entender a forma da resposta para ajustar a tempo.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Price elasticity tells us how sharply volume reacts to a change in price." Elasticity is…
options: the degree to which demand responds to a change
the total size of the market
items.why: Elasticity = elasticidade: quão sensível a demanda é a uma variação (de preço, por exemplo).

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Launching the new bag range will partly ___ sales from our existing line rather than only adding new ones."
items.why: To cannibalise = canibalizar: o novo produto rouba demanda de um produto já existente.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "A ___ on day ten means we simply could not fill orders, and some buyers went elsewhere."
items.why: Stock-out = ruptura de estoque: falta de produto para atender aos pedidos.

items.q: "The plan is only a snapshot of a system that keeps moving." A snapshot here means…
options: a picture of one moment in time
items.why: Snapshot = retrato de um momento; captura o sistema num instante, não seu movimento contínuo.

items.q: "As the quarter unfolds, we compare actuals against the curve." To unfold means to…
options: develop or play out over time
be measured only at the end
items.why: To unfold = desenrolar-se: os fatos se desdobram gradualmente ao longo do tempo.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de planejamento de demanda. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "None of these tweaks will move the needle on total volume." This means they will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível — aqui, negado.

items.q: "We expect the new SKU to eat into the margins of the old line." To eat into means to…
items.why: Eat into = corroer, reduzir aos poucos algo (margens, estoque, tempo).

items.q: "Let's not lock in the price before we've seen the elasticity data." To lock in means to…
options: fix or commit to something firmly
items.why: Lock in = travar, fixar de forma comprometida, difícil de reverter depois.

items.q: "If sales slow, we can dial back the promotion within a week." To dial back means to…
items.why: Dial back = diminuir a intensidade, moderar — sem necessariamente encerrar.

items.q: "When reality diverges from the plan, a good team can course-correct quickly." To course-correct means to…
options: adjust direction in response to new information
items.why: Course-correct = corrigir o rumo: ajustar a rota conforme a realidade muda.
